verdict.tagline: A legendary reimagining with incredible gunplay and a sluggish final stretch.
for_you_if: you love classic shooters modernized with tight mechanics
you want tactical enemy combat encounters
not_for_you_if: you will experience technical instability and crashes
you dislike long drawn-out late-game chapters
you struggle with maze-like level design

distortion_flags.sentence: Approval ratings climb steadily from early players encountering hurdles to long-term fans embracing the full campaign.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Reviewers note janky movement, menu navigation hurdles, and initial technical instability.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the movement and jumping mechanics feel janky or differ from the original game, such as the inability to bunny hop.

citations.review_text:
A reasonably impressive fan project and quality remake of the antiquated classic that is [i]Half-Life[/i], [i]Black Mesa[/i] stumbles only when the Source engine does, which...was quite a lot, actually. 
Still, the janky movement, jumping and interaction will lead the player nicely into [i]Half-Life 2[/i], assuming that you're in it to follow the 'full' arc of the narrative available.
As an entry point to the series, you could do much worse than this, but I freely admit that my thumbs up is a shaky one. Valve lured me onto Steam with the Orange Box like so many others, but my nostalgia for Gordon Freeman was not enough to draw me into this beyond the first few missions.

If you love Half-Life, remakes, or games on the Source engine, you'll probably enjoy yourself.
boring, and you cant even bhop like in the original

claims.claim: Reviewers describe certain sections, particularly Xen and Interloper, as overly prolonged and dragging on.

citations.review_text:
Its a good remake—great even—but there are many parts that became a gigantic pain in the balls. Interloper is why I would never replay this; its way too long and is aggressively boring. Aside from having the ridiculous puzzles that require great effort to make 3 feet of advancement, there are multiple collision errors here where you can clip into a mesh and you're screwed unless you noclip or reload. I have also had the issue of control freezing completely for no reason, but this was only on Interloper. There's this enemy spam that happens which is boring but I suppose is true to the original, but anyway. 

The entire game up to and including Xen was very cool. Gonarch's Lair was fine. Interloper was bad. Nihilanth was pretty cool and it ran really well overall on poverty hardware and looked good. What else can I say?
... why is zen 3 times longer, they took what was already the longest part of the game, and made it take up of twice of the game's runtime proportionally

What can I say, it's both a really good game and a wonderfully faithful recreation of the og half life in a better look and feel

xen was too long tho :(

An excellent reimagining of the original Half-Life. In addition to its vastly improved graphics, the game also expands upon the original by adding new sections and trimming some of the old ones. Most of these changes benefit the game, with the exception of the final third, which takes place in Xen. There, the initial excitement over the visuals is undermined by uninteresting puzzles and repetitive environments. However, the rest of the game feels significantly better, especially when it comes to the gunplay, the redesigned environments, and the new soundtrack.
Was really enjoyable until Xen, which kind of derailed all of my enjoyment with it. 7/10, up until Xen it was about an 8.5
An absolute masterpiece, but XEN is stretched WAY TOO LONG.

Game is really good but the Xen chapters have butt cheeks level design and it drags on too much. Without the Xen, it's good. But with it, it's mediocre at best. Still an enjoyable experience never the less. Not better than the original, but a nice way to experience it in a different way.
Solid remake but Xen part is still the worst gaming experience of my life

An overall fun reimagining of Half-Life, with great visuals and flow even if purists can point out some valid things wrong with it. The first half of Xen is beautiful. The second half kind of sucks, perhaps implying that it's impossible for any developer to get Xen truly right.

I didn't really like the original half life 1 but I tried black mesa. which made it 100% better. this game looked so beautiful I really liked Xen but it had problems it was too long. 

I give it a 9/10

Where to begin? I saw this years ago well before I had a computer. I was very much interested as Half-Life is my favorite game of all time. I am sad they didn't base it off the hd models or at least have that as an option. I say that as I grew up with the PS2 version. Overall I enjoyed myself.

I thought the changes were interesting. A lot of the environment looked very fleshed out and the facility looked far better and more cohesive. However there were questionable changes as well. I liked On A Rail being shortened but I hate that Interloper was extended so much. It was cool at first but it started to drag and felt like it greatly overstayed its welcome. I'd say the entirely of the Xen levels were a smidge too long.

Also seems like someone on the team really loves Barnacles, Itcthyasaurs and Gargantuas. Did you guys really need to make the Itcthyasaurs so freaking scary? I did get over it rather quickly but good Lord the introduction to them in Apprehension was terrifying. Also I don't recall the HECU being so annoying to fight.

Overall I'd say this was a decent remake. I do wonder how VALvE would have done it though.

Nice remake of old Half Life. What should I say? Well, the part in allien realm was too long...can't remember if it was like that in old game as well. Still, cool remake. I enjoyed it a lot. Classic HL.

claims.claim: The level design can feel like a maze, requiring players to search for hidden vents or the single correct path.

citations.review_text: This game is incredibly unintuitive. It feels like I'm fight with the map design more so than the actual enemies. If this game is a remake of the original, then I dread every having to play it.

While Half Life is considered a masterpiece in gaming, it's hard to understand why that is with todays standards.

Black Mesa is a faithful remake of the original 1998 Half Life, meaning that it keeps all the issues the game had. While I'm sure the game must've been insanely fun in 1998, it's really hard to recommend nowadays - Some chapters and levels drag on for way too long making it feel like a chore to get on through with the story. The level design is rather poor, it's a lot of seeking where to go but with only one correct path in a big maze like level (This gets annoying quickly, finding a hidden vent that you've been looking for 10 minutes doesn't feel rewarding at all). The combat is really simple and extremely repetitive, this would've been alright if it didn't feel like the enemies were simply placed to slow you down throughout the levels.

Where this game really shines in my opinion is when there's downtime - Being able to talk with the scientists and helping them feels extremely refreshing when you've just gone through an endless maze with a half baked motive of "Go launch the rocket, Gordon. I don't know why but I've been told you have to". The graphics are also really good considering this runs on source, although the performance can be a little unstable sometimes - Crashes can also be frequent on lower memory systems.

Overall I feel like this game is a relic of what video games used to be, it's definitely not bad but it's hard to recommend when there's so many better story FPS games out there.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Praise for gunplay and tactical enemies sits alongside complaints of dragged-out chapters and software crashes.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the late-game and Xen chapters feel overly long, stretched out, or tedious.

citations.review_text: I had a lot of fun. I love the story, the environments, and how atmospheric it all is. The game has great art direction, it looks great. The only thing I would change is the fact that some parts feel too long, where nothing new happens in terms of gameplay or story development.

Apart from overly long last levels and occasional mechanical clunkiness, that was a very solid experience! Well done to the developers for their dedication and skill. The game has a very old school feel - it provides a great sense of place, allows you to explore in your own pace and doesn't rush you for the most part. Weapons feel and sound nice. Combat vs. military guys was simple but engaging. I have spoken!

Really impressive how they updated a classic but stayed true to the source. Some techical issues here and there but nothing major. Lots of nostalgia here but the new material was well done. The Interloper level could probably have been trimmed a bit but what they did with Xen was excellent. Well worth grabbing but play the original first.

This is a really good homage to the original Half Life.  I did try HL1 a little while ago, but how the game has aged was offputting.

Black Mesa managed to recapture that primal fear I felt as a child while playing back in 1999, and what they changed Xen too, was a beautiful thing.

However, the Xen part of the game seemed to last longer than the earth part of the game... was that just me?

Lets call it a tribute to Halflife 1 and it's great. It's an upgraded version of the game with some changes. Weapons and enemies are the same if I recall correctly after more than 20 years. Enemies have the same great AI and will flush you out if you are behind something, they will not run into your crosshair. There are almost always several ways to approach the situation. 

Graphic is good, sound and music are a bit better. The story is the same. Maps are a bit different. What is not the same is Xen. When I arrived there for the first time I was taken away I think more than when I played Halflife all those years ago. There were a lot of great ideas and situations. But it quickly turned into a chore because of its length. And we are not playing games to feel as if it is a chore. You will be able to read a lot of complaints on the internet about it. And it is really so. I wish it would have been shorter. I know there are some shortcuts, but I didn’t find them. Bosses are great. Just too bad Xen is so loooooong. 

I wouldn’t want to play the game as a whole again, but I have played a few parts again as they were really great.

I would 100% have recommended this if not for three things:

1. Xen is insanely long now. I thought the complaints were just about the Xen chapter itself, but no, I mean Xen, Gonarch's Lair, and Interloper are so long it's honestly a bit exhausting considering what two of the achievements require.

2. Speaking of those two achievements. Jesus Christ. The reward truly does not justify the headache of carting two items from earlier in the game to the very end of the game. Not to mention you hit a point where you can't bring along both anymore so you're left to slog through most of Interloper and then defeat the big bad all over again. This wouldn't be an issue if not for number 3.

3. The two items required themselves. The hat may as well have a rocket attached to it with how often it'll just go off on it's own adventure, often times out of reach or off of the map, and good luck getting the pizza box through most small spaces. It's big, clunky, and vents absolutely hate it.

If you want to play the game one time through and ignore the two most tedious achievements I've ever dealt with, then it's a great game. If you want to 100% the game then I'd recommend just playing Half-Life 1. Graphics aside the original still holds up really well.
Extremely awesome remake of the OG genre-bending game. Only have one complaint: it's a bit too long. I wish Xen was cut down to like 1-1.5 hours max. Otherwise, fantastic.
reimagine the half life as complete new expreience. beautiful graphics. but last 3 chapters feel too long.

An absolutely amazing remake of a classic that improves on almost all aspects of the original. Half-Life is one of my favorite games of all time and I can't believe that I waited so long to complete Black Mesa.

Black Mesa truly feels like how the original Half-Life would be made if it were created in the modern era. The amount of time and effort put in to Xen specifically really shows how much Crowbar Collective adore Half-Life. I definitely recommend this 1000000%.

My only gripe is that the conveyor belt section during the Interloper chapter went on wayyyyy too long. Also, some of the optimization settings could be improved on. Other than that, the game is phenomenal.

Yes, but also no.....this game is great ............UNTIL.......Xen, then just no. it's no good. 

If you even THINK about achievements - absolutely no. Completely ruins the experience to be honest. 

Play it like normal and consider the going to Xen the end of the game then it is  10/10 --- doing Xen is long, tedious, frustrating, difficult, and just awful to be honest -2/10.

Pretty much agree with general consensus. It's incredible to see how the original Half Life has been taken and truly transformed into what feels like a different game but also sort of the same game too. The gunplay is solid here, with all of the weapons looking, sounding, and feeling great. Different from the OG ones, for sure, and I do miss the og pistol, that thing just feels great. The music is lacking a little bit at times but is overall quite good. The ambient music stuff really works but the electronic stuff is kind of weak. 

Xen is fascinating, because parts of it are great, like exploring the abandoned xen science outposts is maybe, genuinely, my favorite part of the whole game. I've always loved DOOM 3 and these parts for sure remind me of when you're exploring hell in DOOM 3. But as xen drags on, it just gets horrible and worse and worse. Like, to the point that I almost end up wondering if the xen here is worse than the OG half life. And obviously the soldier ai got nuked, which was one of literally the best aspects of the OG half life. It's heavy give and take with this one, but I love it for what it is and what it at times attempts but fails to be as well. It's clear that the devs have huge love for the original game, which is what really matters to me, I want Half Life as a franchise to continue, and to continue being relevant, and this game is one of the best ways that that has managed to happen.

I genuinely cant find many flaws with the game. 
The gameplay is timeless, albeit for younger gamers it might feel dated but .. give it a try and see the game through a lense of a different era of gaming this was impressive back then and still holds up today even tho it might deviate from the norm. 
Only mods i had installed was a gun mod for modernized sounds / animations and rather more satisfying gunplay and a script making it possible to walk by pressing "Alt" 

The atmosphere is phenomenal, the soundtrack exceptional and placed just as well, for every rather quiet gameplay focused moment you get a big setpiece moment / establishing shot or a song that sets the mood for the upcoming battle / view or what not. 

Exploration is done well and leaves just enough stuff hidden that looking for little extra hiding spots or secrets tends to be rewarded with ressources. 

I also love how the game doesnt fall down the common trap of singleplayer shooters where some guns eventually get obsolete, the starting pistol still has a lot of uses even in the lategame. 
The lategame tho .. oof .. its definetely stretched out a little bit too much and although it offers quite a few "cool moments" theres also just as many moments where you go "but .. why tho?" and things that could have been designed way shorter. The final few fights are just rather frantic and lack the sort of "vibe" 90% of the rest of the game had where playing smart, semi tactical and creative was rewarded while the final stages of the game are filled with more cheapshot backstabby encounters or push through encounters where there isnt a lot of margin for precise let alone methodical gameplay and its mostly just rushing run and gun action with mostly just 2 weapons because they for some reason eventually stop giving you ammo for the actually satisfying guns and you get rather lame - ish sci fi slob beam / laser rifle weapons which tend to be cool when you first aquire them and they are absurdly powerful a…

The first half is very cool and well-paced. Xen starts off strong with stunning visuals and fantastic atmosphere, impressive.

Xen boss battles are bad. They are long, repetitive, and boring; the collision detection makes those encounters worse. I was constantly getting stuck in some rocks during a battle and couldn't move until the boss accidentally broke them. I just wanted the game to be over sooner

Well, I have just finished Black Mesa for the first time... and I am mightily impressed.

For me, it won't replace the original, since it's one of my favourite games and I grew up with it. There are so many little quirks and funny things about that game that cannot be duplicated. Not to mention: the historical aspect of it. Black Mesa does a fine job reminding me of why I love the Half-Life universe, and to me, it's an excellent re-imagining. Because that's what it is. It's not a replacement, it's a new perspective on old ideas, while also adding new ideas of its own. [b]It's a great game that stands on its own.[/b]

The new voice acting, music and sound effects are all very good. I love how clear the sound of the weapons are and how they sound when you reload them. Crystal clear. The music pays tribute to the original soundtrack while also doing its own things. The voice acting can also be unintentionally funny sometimes, as the scientists and guards seem overtly calm considering everything that's going on! Regarding the Marines: I don't know how they would sound in real life, but they felt real in this game. In many ways, Black Mesa humanizes the Marines, even making them sound scared at times. Small things like this adds greatly to the experience!

I did encounter quite a few bugs, mostly because I kept getting stuck on items or on the ground, so it's not a perfect experience. Some of the Xen stages are also pretty difficult, which was a bit frustrating. Thankfully, they are at the end of the game!

[b]And I just have to say it:[/b] The Xen stages alone are worth the price of admission. They are absolutely gorgeous. I love how alive it feels and the use of colours. More colours in gaming! While the rest of the game won't replace the original for me, the Xen stages probably will, because they just feel so real.

[h2] In conclusion:[/h2]
Black Mesa is a great game, right up there with the official releases. But... [b]DO NOT FORGET THE ORIGINAL![/b]

When I arrived there for the first time I was taken away I think more than when I played Halflife all those years ago. There were a lot of great ideas and situations. But it quickly turned into a chore because of its length. And we are not playing games to feel as if it is a chore. You will be able to read a lot of complaints on the internet about it. And it is really so. I wish it would have been shorter. I know there are some shortcuts, but I didn’t find them. Bosses are great. Just too bad Xen is so loooooong. 

I wouldn’t want to play the game as a whole again, but I have played a few parts again as they were really great.

Where do I even begin? This game took what made Half-Life 1 good and just made it better, with great AI, a complete overhaul on graphics, and they changed some parts of the chapters and even changed them for the better because chapters 7 and 8 are actually doable and you're not scratching your head trying to figure out where to go. But I will say, the AI are so aggressive in this game; they do not let up on you. But I love this and how a remake should be done.

citations.review_text:
Black Mesa is a wonderfully well-made remake of Half-Life. Crowbar Collective took everything that made the original great and went above and beyond in recreating it, improving what was already there while also adding substantial new content.

The most notable example is Xen. In the original Half-Life, Xen was roughly an hour long and felt rushed, much like the final season of Game of Thrones. In Black Mesa, it is transformed into an epic four-to-five-hour adventure.

There really isn’t much to complain about. Sure, there are still plenty of loading screens, but I chalk that up to the game running on the Source engine, which is the only acceptable engine for a Half-Life remake, so it gets a pass.

I did encounter one game-breaking bug toward the end. A passageway became blocked, and nothing I tried fixed it. It seemed like an event had triggered prematurely, trapping me in the area leading up to it. Thankfully, loading a recent save allowed me to get around it.

It is absolutely wild to think that this began as a fan-made project and spent 16 years in development. In the end, the result was a masterpiece.

Well, I have just finished Black Mesa for the first time... and I am mightily impressed.

For me, it won't replace the original, since it's one of my favourite games and I grew up with it. There are so many little quirks and funny things about that game that cannot be duplicated. Not to mention: the historical aspect of it. Black Mesa does a fine job reminding me of why I love the Half-Life universe, and to me, it's an excellent re-imagining. Because that's what it is. It's not a replacement, it's a new perspective on old ideas, while also adding new ideas of its own. [b]It's a great game that stands on its own.[/b]

The new voice acting, music and sound effects are all very good. I love how clear the sound of the weapons are and how they sound when you reload them. Crystal clear. The music pays tribute to the original soundtrack while also doing its own things. The voice acting can also be unintentionally funny sometimes, as the scientists and guards seem overtly calm considering everything that's going on! Regarding the Marines: I don't know how they would sound in real life, but they felt real in this game. In many ways, Black Mesa humanizes the Marines, even making them sound scared at times. Small things like this adds greatly to the experience!

I did encounter quite a few bugs, mostly because I kept getting stuck on items or on the ground, so it's not a perfect experience. Some of the Xen stages are also pretty difficult, which was a bit frustrating. Thankfully, they are at the end of the game!

[b]And I just have to say it:[/b] The Xen stages alone are worth the price of admission. They are absolutely gorgeous. I love how alive it feels and the use of colours. More colours in gaming! While the rest of the game won't replace the original for me, the Xen stages probably will, because they just feel so real.

[h2] In conclusion:[/h2]
Black Mesa is a great game, right up there with the official releases. But... [b]DO NOT FORGET THE ORIGINAL![/b]

citations.review_text:
[h2] Disclaimer: This is my first Half-Life Game so far, I am planning on playing the original Half-Life after this, and then I will the rest of the series accordingly. Some may say that was the wrong choice, as I have seen online, but oh well. [/h2]

This was a really cool and good game. I just completed it, and it took me a surprisingly long time (it did not actually take me over 100 hours, I accidentally AFK'd for 3 days at one point, it actually took me a little over 21 hours). It was really fun and exciting, but the puzzles made me actually think while playing in a game for once, which usually isn't my cup of tea, forcing me to look at walkthroughs a couple times, but I got used to it over time and actually started having fun figuring out the, albeit relatively simple, puzzles.

I am not gonna go into it too detailed, all I will say is that the game has some pacing issues at some points (I don't know if that has to do with the original Half-Life or is exclusive to this game), and it can especially start dragging a bit in the last quarter (which is definitely exclusive to this game since I've heard the Xen portion is fully new).

The soundtrack for this game is also really fun. Although I wish the songs were a bit more prevalent throughout, the rarity of music in the game makes songs hit so much harder when they do come on, especially during boss battles.

Major spoilers incoming, [spoiler] the boss battles are so fun, especially the one with the Controllers. Gornach is also fun, but it can drag a bit. The most anticlimactic boss battle was Nihlanth, which had like no music and was incredibly easy compared to the rest. Also I'm an idiot and thought that by denying G-Man's offer of employment I would get to fight him, that was not the case. [/spoiler]

Anyway, I had a lot of fun playing this game, and I honestly think it was a great introduction to the franchise, even if it's not made by Valve. I will be playing the original Half-Life before moving onto…

Great reimagination of Half-Life 1. The Surface Tension and Xenian chapters have been massively expanded, so I would definitely recommend a playthrough for HL1 veterans. Also 'fixes' On A Rail by just cutting a massive portion off it. Weapons and combat is satisfying though it can get overwhelming on harder difficulties. PC Spec requirements are quite high but if you have a powerful PC, its worth it. 9.5/10

claims.claim: Reviewers report technical issues, specifically mentioning game crashes tied to high entity or prop counts and general stability problems near the end of the game.

citations.review_text: Parts of this game are amazing, but parts of it are really, really bad and for every moment where you're blown away by some outstanding music, graphics or gameplay  there's more where you're feeling more like "oh not THIS again" or the controls glitch, or the level design just feels spiteful as if the devs are getting the huff that you're nearly at the end and want to make sure that you can't  enjoy beating it. Sorry if that sounds harsh but that's exactly what it feels like. Interloper is an ordeal not a game....oh and then it crashes and can't get to the end anyway, magic. The pinned bug list and number of workarounds should tell you everything you need to know, the game has flashes of actual brilliance but it's also just SO ♥♥♥♥ a lot of the time.
Very good remaster but some times crashes when there's too much props/entites.
